text: You built an app.
Somebody, someday, will ask what it's worth.
Most calculators hand you a number.
And keep the reasoning to themselves.
So here is the reasoning.
Your revenue is a surface.
Price on one side, customers on the other.
Double either one, and you double the area.
But only one of them is free.
So where does that put you?
On the pricing ladder, Spotify is a mouse: €2 a month per user.
Shopify is a deer, at €75.
Salesforce is a whale.
Your price per customer decides your trade.
Who sells, who onboards, how many customers you will ever need.
But growing is not enough.
Direct costs, acquisition, fixed costs: each one takes its share.
What a buyer pays for is what remains at the bottom.
No profit, no multiple.
Then nine lines build that multiple.
Churn. Growth. Retention. Client concentration.
And how much of the company walks out of the door with you.
Every one of them, named.
Colombes. Free. No sign-up.
